'''''Abrophyllum''''' ([[synonym (taxonomy)|syn.]]: ''Brachynema'' F.Muell.) is a [[monotypic]] genus of [[flowering plant]]s in the family [[Saxifragaceae]] ''sensu lato'' according to [[Adolf Engler|Engler, A.]] in Engler & [[K. A. E. Prantl|Prantl]] and Schulze-Menz, G. K. in [[Hans Melchior|Melchior]], 1964; placed in Subfamily Escallonioideae, Tribe Cuttsieae, it is closely related to ''[[Cuttsia]]''. In the [[APG II system]] ''Abrophyllum'' is placed in family [[Rousseaceae]].

The sole species is '''''Abrophyllum ornans'''''. Its common name is '''native hydrangea''', but it does not have great affinity with the true [[hydrangea]].

==Classification==
It is also classified in [[Escalloniaceae]] (by [[John Hutchinson (botanist)|Hutchinson]] 1967; [[Rolf Dahlgren|Dahlgren]]; [[Robert F. Thorne|Thorne]]), [[Grossulariaceae]] ([[Arthur Cronquist|Cronquist]] 1988), [[Carpodetaceae]] ([[APG system|APG I]] 1998, [[Kubitzki system|Kubitzki]] 2007<ref>{{cite book|author1= Gustafsson, M.H.G. |chapter=Carpodetaceae |editor1=Kubitzki, K. |title = The Families and Genera of Vascular Plants|editor2= Kadereit, J. W. |editor3=Jeffrey, C. |volume=8 |publisher=Springer-Verlag |place=Berlin| year = 2007| isbn = 978-3-540-31050-1}}</ref>), [[Rousseaceae]] ([[APG II system|APG II]] 2003, [[Alexey B. Shipunov|Shipunov]] 2005, Thorne & Reveal 2007<ref>Thorne, R. F. & Reveal, J. L. 2007. An updated classification of the class Magnolipsida ("Angiospermae"). Bot. Rev. 73(2): 67-182.</ref> and Heywood ''et al.'' 2007<ref>{{cite book|author = Heywood, V. H. |author2=Brummitt, R. K. |author3=Culham, A. |author4=Seberg, O. |title = Flowering Plant Families of the World| publisher = Firefly Books| year = 2007| location = Richmond Hill, Ontario, Canada|isbn = 978-1-55407-206-4}}</ref>), or even in its own family '''Abrophyllaceae''' [[Takenoshin Nakai|Nakai]] ([[Reveal system|Reveal]] and [[Takhtajan]] 1997).

==Distribution==
It is native to Australia ([[New South Wales]] and [[Queensland]]). Its habitat is warm-temperate and subtropical rainforest, especially along smaller watercourses or in gullies on poorer soils. The natural range of distribution is from the [[Illawarra]] region of New South Wales to the [[McIlwraith Range]] in far north Queensland.<ref>* [[Alexander Floyd|Floyd, Alexander G.]], ''Rainforest Trees of Mainland South-eastern Australia'', Inkata Press 1989, {{ISBN|0-909605-57-2}}, page 126</ref>

==Description==
[[Image:Abrophyllum Nat Pfl.jpg|thumb|right|''Abrophyllum ornans'' in Engler & Prantl]]
Shrubs or small trees to {{cvt|8|m}} high; leaves simple, mostly {{cvt|10|-|20|cm}} long, {{cvt|3|-|8|cm}} wide, alternate, large, [[lanceolate]], long-acuminate, subserrate; without [[stipule]]s, [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]] {{cvt|20|-|40|mm|1}} long. Flowers in terminal or axillary [[Cyme (botany)|cymes]], yellowish. [[sepal|Calyx]] is short (c. {{cvt|2|mm|1}} long.), tubular, lobes usually 5 or sometimes 6, deciduous. Petals {{cvt|4|-|5|mm|1}} long, usually 5 or sometimes 6, valvate, spreading, deciduous. [[Stamen]]s usually 5 or sometimes 6, inserted on the margin of the inconspicuous nectary disk; [[anther]]s broad oblong; filaments very short. [[Gynoecium]] of 5 [[carpel]]s, [[wiktionary:receptacle|receptacle]] patelliform. [[Ovary (plants)|Ovary]] superior, 5-locular, with numerous axile [[ovule]]s, [[carpel|stigma]] sessile, 5-lobed. Fruit are oblong, black [[Berry (botany)|berries]] about {{cvt|8|-|12|mm|1}} long and {{cvt|5|-|7|mm|2}} wide, crowned by the stigma, many-seeded; seeds small, subglobose, testa deeply latticed; [[embryo]] very small; [[endosperm]] fleshy and oily.

==Uses==
Sometimes (locally){{where?|date=October 2024}} cultivated for its ornamental foliage and fruits.{{cn|date=October 2024}}
